item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 032329
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sat Oct 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west-northwest of the main
Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a few hundred
miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form late this weekend or
early next week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is expected to form during the middle to
latter portion of next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Blake

item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 040252
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  28
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026
 
...RACHEL STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY AS IT CONTINUES WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.0N 112.8W
ABOUT 275 MI...440 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 20.0 North, longitude 112.8 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this motion is
expected to prevail though the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased near 90 mph (150 km/h) with 
higher gusts.  Rachel should start to weaken on Sunday before some 
re-strengthening is possible on Monday or Tuesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of west-central Mexico through the weekend and the Baja California
Peninsula through Monday. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Blake

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 28
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026 
612 
WTPZ43 KNHC 040253
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  28
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026
 
Satellite imagery suggests that Rachel's convective organization has 
improved since the previous advisory. The hurricane now shows a 
large, defined eye surrounded by a symmetric ring of deep convection 
with cloud top temperatures as cold as -80 C. The latest subjective 
Dvorak estimate from TAFB came in at T4.5/77 kt, closely mirroring 
many of the UW-CIMSS objective intensity estimates that range from 
70 to 97 kt. Based on a compromise of these data, the initial 
intensity is raised to 80 kt.
 
The initial motion continues west-northwestward, or 300/4 kt. 
Rachel's slow motion over the next two days will be governed by a 
ridge extending southwestward from a mid- to upper-level high over 
the western United States. Rachel is forecast to accelerate slightly 
after 60 h, continuing on a west to west-northwestward trajectory 
through the remainder of the forecast period. The updated NHC track 
forecast was largely unchanged from the previous advisory, roughly 
in between the corrected consensus (HCCA) and the Google DeepMind 
ensemble mean.

Rachel is forecast to experience weakening in the next 24 h as it 
enters an unfavorable environment of cooler sea surface temperatures 
associated with Hurricane Polo's cold wake, moderate northwesterly 
vertical wind shear, and mid-level dry air. However, the cyclone 
could be at the early stage of acquiring structural characteristics 
typical of an annular hurricane, as outer rainbands have dissipated 
in favor of a thick, uniform central core.  This could temper any 
weakening, as long as the easterly wind shear remains relatively 
low, and the new forecast is a bit higher than the last one.  As 
Rachel continues on a westward motion, vertical wind shear 
decreases, allowing environmental conditions to improve and offering 
the chance for some re-intensification through 72 h. Beyond 72 h, 
however, Rachel should encounter an even drier air mass, with 
mid-level relative humidity values dipping below 40 percent, 
alongside SSTs dropping below 26 C.  These conditions are forecast 
to cause the cyclone to gradually weaken through at the end of the 
forecast period, similar to the last advisory.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
